title: Certificate Transparency Version 2.0
algorithm_class: Merkle append-only transparency log with signed tree heads, SCTs and inclusion/consistency proofs
supported_guarantee: Tamper-evident append-only logging: Merkle tree heads (RFC 9162 Sec. 2.1) with inclusion proofs (Sec. 2.1.3) and consistency proofs (Sec. 2.1.4) let any auditor detect log splitting or retroactive edit; the arm-B3 source semantics.
limitations_vs_candidate: Integrity only, never confidentiality or minimization: entries are public by design, RFC 9162 Sec. 8.1.4 flags fetching inclusion proofs as a privacy leak, and the RFC defines no retention schedule, no purpose binding, no attacker-advantage bound and no forensic answerability endpoint, so CL-1 separation is not pre-empted.
mechanism_analysis: Registry ct9162 anchors PST arm B3 and claim CL-1; upstream certificate-transparency-go (HEAD bc63c417c7be, Apache-2.0 LICENSE, verified live 2026-11-15) implements exactly the RFC log semantics, while transparency-dev/merkle (HEAD c39fbf350a40, Apache-2.0, verified live) supplies the RFC 6962-style tree algorithm. The mechanism is witnessed append-only integrity: an editor cannot quietly drop or rewrite a leaf without an inconsistent tree head, but a legitimate audit reader still reads everything ever appended - the candidate's frontier separates committed proof from recoverable content, which RFC 9162 neither defines nor bounds.

title: Macaroons: Cookies with Contextual Caveats for Decentralized Authorization in the Cloud
algorithm_class: HMAC caveat-chain contextual capability credentials with first-class attenuation
supported_guarantee: Unforgeable context-bound authorization: caveats (actor, purpose, expiry, nonce) are bound into an HMAC chain so delegation attenuates without key sharing and verification fails closed outside the caveat set; the B1-digest lineage and T3 purpose-binding source.
limitations_vs_candidate: Authorization-time scoping only: caveat satisfaction is evaluated at presentation, nothing bounds what an audit store retains, no retention map or decay schedule exists, and a satisfied caveat grants reading whatever content the store holds - no linkability or attribute-inference endpoint is defined, so CL-2 separation is not pre-empted.
mechanism_analysis: Registry macaroons14 anchors PST claim CL-2 and the HMAC identifier surface ReceiptMin minimizes; upstream libmacaroons (HEAD ca0211d8633c, BSD-3-Clause, verified live 2026-11-15) is the authors' reference implementation, with pymacaroons v0.13.0 (tag -> 06b55110eda2, MIT, verified live via ls-remote) as an independent cross-check. Mechanistically the HMAC chain binds the caveat context to the token, so it commits an event to a purpose - precisely the ReceiptMin commitment primitive - but it stores no minimization policy: whatever plaintext sits behind a valid capability remains fully recoverable, which is the gap the reconstruction-versus-linkability frontier measures.

title: Zanzibar: Google’s Consistent, Global Authorization System
algorithm_class: Consistency-aware distributed ReBAC authorization with zookie version tokens
supported_guarantee: Globally consistent permission evaluation: zookies provide bounded-staleness consistency tokens, monotonic snapshot reads and externally consistent check-after-write (Pang et al. 2019, Sec. 2.3-2.4); the CL-7 consistency reference.
limitations_vs_candidate: Governs permission-tuple evaluation only: no post-retention audit metadata exposure bound, no retention or key-deletion semantics, no forensic reconstruction measure; a check admitted at the right snapshot says nothing about what retained artifacts leak to a compromised read-only audit reader, so CL-7 separation is not pre-empted.
mechanism_analysis: Registry zanzibar19 anchors PST claim CL-7: consistency-aware authorization is the closest published mechanism that could plausibly imply audit-retention guarantees, and the claim fails if it already provides matching exposure bounds. Mechanistically zookies sequence tuple writes and gate permission re-evaluation - a temporal property of the authorization state - whereas PST's endpoint is a property of retained audit content under a read-only reader privilege; no Google official code release exists (the executable Zanzibar semantics are covered by the openfga row), so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN and consistency claims are measured against B2/B3 semantics, never assumed away.

title: FHIR R5 Consent, AuditEvent, Provenance resources
algorithm_class: Interoperability standard defining Consent, AuditEvent and Provenance resource structures
supported_guarantee: Structured vocabulary for consent scope, audit events and provenance chains: AuditEvent/Provenance record who acted under which consent reference, and Consent binds data use to declared purposes (R5, 2023); the CL-3 schema reference.
limitations_vs_candidate: Defines structures and exchange semantics, not guarantees: no quantitative reconstructability endpoint, no retention-decay schedule semantics, no attacker-exposure bound and no oracle scoring - FHIR conformance is not forensic sufficiency or privacy (ledger relation: FHIR compliance is not clinical safety), so CL-3 separation is not pre-empted.
mechanism_analysis: Registry fhir5 anchors PST claim CL-3: standard clinical audit schemas are the obvious prior art a reviewer would cite against a new forensic endpoint, and the claim dies if an AuditEvent/Provenance retention profile already specifies equivalent measurable reconstructability bounds. Mechanistically the R5 resources fix field structure and referential integrity - who, what, when, under which consent - but leave retention policy, minimization and exposure entirely to implementers; a specification has no runnable implementation to cite (reference servers are conformance servers, not the standard), so UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN is the honest status and the row supplies field vocabulary only.

title: MUSE: Machine Unlearning Six-Way Evaluation for Language Models
algorithm_class: Six-axis empirical evaluation framework for machine unlearning of language models
supported_guarantee: Distinguishes unlearning from future-disclosure prevention and from utility retention, and measures each axis empirically for models and derived content (2024); the CL-4 evaluation-boundary reference.
limitations_vs_candidate: Operates on model weights and model-derived content, not on retained ledger receipts or audit stores: no append-only commitment, no consent/policy epoch proofs, no read-only audit-reader adversary, and no linkability/attribute-inference axes, so CL-4 separation is not pre-empted.
mechanism_analysis: Registry muse anchors PST claim CL-4: the nearest adjacent evaluation framework, and the claim fails if MUSE axes already capture retained-audit reconstruction equivalence. Mechanistically MUSE scores how completely a model's learned influence is removed (knowledge-extraction and privacy-leakage probes against the model), which is influence removal from parameters; ReceiptMin scores how much decision-relevant forensic content survives deliberate minimization of an append-only audit store - a data-artifact property, not a learned-parameter property - so the axes are disjoint by construction. The registry records no official runnable code release, hence UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN with the falsification test still standing.

title: Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) Architecture
algorithm_class: Normative attestation architecture: attester, evidence, verifier and relying-party roles
supported_guarantee: Strict role and evidence taxonomy (RFC 9334 Sec. 3-4): evidence is produced by the attester about itself, verified by a verifier, and consumed as attestation results; prevents conflating a bare digest with hardware attestation; the CL-5 evidence-role reference.
limitations_vs_candidate: Defines who produces and verifies evidence, not what may be retained or reconstructed: no minimization schedule, no linkability bound, no forensic answerability metric and no audit-reader adversary model, so CL-5 separation is not pre-empted.
mechanism_analysis: Registry rats9334 anchors PST claim CL-5 and the threat-model boundary that a digest is never treated as authorization: the RATS vocabulary is what keeps ReceiptMin's S1 event commitments from being read as attestation of clinical correctness. Mechanistically RFC 9334 structures evidence flows between roles, which shapes the PST oracle/actor authority split, but it is a normative architecture document with no executable implementation to cite - any code would be a third-party toy - so the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN and it fixes the evidence boundary rather than serving as a runnable arm.

title: Guide to Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) Definition and Considerations
algorithm_class: Normative ABAC vocabulary and design-considerations guidance (standard)
supported_guarantee: Formal attribute-based access-control vocabulary (subject/resource/action/environment attributes including purpose-of-use) and policy-composition guidance (NIST SP 800-162, updated 2019); the CL-6 purpose-attribute reference.
limitations_vs_candidate: Vocabulary and design considerations only: no algorithm, no retention or decay semantics, no measurable retained-read endpoint, and no exposure bound under a compromised audit reader, so CL-6 separation is not pre-empted.
mechanism_analysis: Registry nistabac anchors PST claim CL-6 and supplies the normative attribute terms (purpose, environment, operation) with which PST states receipt fields and the ex-ante frozen forensic query set. Mechanistically SP 800-162 defines how attributes compose into access decisions - an authorization-time activity - and is silent on what an audit store may retain afterward or what a reader may infer from residue; a standard cannot be a runnable baseline, so UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN is correct and the CL-6 differentiation is measured against arms B1-B3, not against the guide.

title: Ethics and Governance of Artificial Intelligence for Health
algorithm_class: Normative ethics and governance guidance for health AI
supported_guarantee: Normative principles - purpose limitation, accountability, auditability of health AI systems - that motivate minimized, purpose-bound audit retention (WHO 2021); the CL-8 governance reference.
limitations_vs_candidate: Normative guidance, not empirical evidence: prescribes no measurable endpoint, no protocol, no baseline arms and no exposure bound; cannot confirm or refute a frontier claim, so CL-8 separation is not pre-empted.
mechanism_analysis: Registry who21 anchors PST claim CL-8: governance guidance is the rhetorical source of the purpose-limitation requirement ReceiptMin operationalizes, and the claim fails if WHO guidance already prescribes a measurable audit-minimization endpoint. Mechanistically the WHO report states principles and recommends governance mechanisms at policy level, deliberately without benchmarks or metrics; a guidance document has nothing runnable to cite, so UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN is the honest status, and PST's contribution is precisely the quantitative measurement the guidance calls for but does not define.

title: OpenFGA: Zanzibar-inspired fine-grained authorization
algorithm_class: Zanzibar-inspired relationship-based authorization (ReBAC) with consistency tokens and fresh evaluation
supported_guarantee: Executable relationship checks with minimize_latency=false consistency tokens and fresh evaluation mode; pinned at tag v1.22.1 (upstream revision 44054f542f64e9b9589dd26a595081b3d2cfd942, Apache-2.0, verified live 2026-11-15); the runnable CL-7 cross-check for RQ2 attacker-privilege gating.
limitations_vs_candidate: Relationship-tuple consistency only: no retained-audit exposure bound, no retention schedule, no forensic query set and no linkability endpoint - consent epochs must be re-encoded externally as tuple attributes, and consistency of a permission check says nothing about residue linkability.
mechanism_analysis: Registry openfga is the executable counterpart of the Zanzibar CL-7 reference: the actual OpenFGA server at pinned v1.22.1 (revision resolved live via ls-remote refs/tags/v1.22.1 on 2026-11-15) can run the RQ2 attacker harness's authorization gating so that privilege checks are real, consistent authorization rather than a stub. Its mechanism - zookie-style tokens over relationship tuples - is orthogonal to the measured frontier: even perfectly consistent admission leaves retained receipt content fully reconstructable to the privileged reader, which is exactly the separation CL-7 asserts; if OpenFGA semantics could encode a matching exposure bound, the claim dies, and it is run at equal budget to test that.

title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
algorithm_class: Agent attack benchmark: indirect prompt injection against tool-integrated LLMs
supported_guarantee: Dataset of direct and indirect injection test cases measuring whether tool-integrated agents execute malicious instructions; establishes the model-layer threat taxonomy that PST's threat model explicitly excludes (X-domain boundary to dispatch-path attacks).
limitations_vs_candidate: Model-layer instruction following only: no audit store, no retention artifact, no read-only audit-reader adversary and no reconstruction or linkability measure; the PST compromised-reader (P1/P2) threat family is disjoint from prompt-injection corpora by design.
mechanism_analysis: Registry injecagent24 is a boundary comparator: it is cited to show the closest real agent-attack benchmark measures a different endpoint (instruction compliance after injection), so PST's forensic-omission and linkability families are neither borrowed nor re-labelled from it. The upstream repo exists, but the row is registered as a taxonomy-only comparator - no MUSE-style code execution in the PST pipeline - so available_code=no reflects its registered non-execution role rather than absence upstream; if InjecAgent already measured post-retention audit reconstructability, the PST threat-model novelty would collapse, and it does not.

title: Full plaintext append-only log (blueprint arm B0; registry baseline full-plaintext-append-only-log)
algorithm_class: Append-only plaintext audit log of all AI health actions; utility upper bound / privacy lower bound
supported_guarantee: Complete retention: every event field is readable forever, so the ex-ante frozen forensic query set is answerable at 1.0 by construction at every retention stage - the utility ceiling every minimization arm is measured against.
limitations_vs_candidate: Privacy lower bound: a compromised read-only audit reader (P1) reads everything, and with auxiliary joins (P2) linkage and attribute-inference advantage are unbounded; no decay, no purpose binding, no minimization - the RQ2 exposure ceiling that ReceiptMin must strictly dominate.
mechanism_analysis: Arm B0 (registry baseline full-plaintext-append-only-log, parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/pst/fixtures/plaintext_log_parity.json, exec_command registered; notes: in-project, not yet run): its scientific role is calibration - B0 defines the RQ1 answerability ceiling and the RQ2 exposure ceiling, so the frontier can only be claimed between these extremes. The implementation does not exist yet in evaluation/venue2027, hence honestly UNAVAILABLE/UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN rather than claiming a run that never happened; comparative claims against B0 stay blocked until the arm runs.

title: Hash-only log or content digests (blueprint arm B1; registry baseline hash-only-log-digests)
algorithm_class: SHA-256 content digests of audit events only; minimal prior-art minimization with weak audit utility
supported_guarantee: Minimal minimization prior art: digests commit events unforgeably while retaining no plaintext payload, so RQ2 exposure is low by content removal - the strongest competing baseline for the RQ2 privacy half, per the novelty contract.
limitations_vs_candidate: Weak audit utility: without commitment-adjacent purpose/epoch proofs, authorization, provenance and commit-eligibility questions return INDETERMINATE, and residual metadata (pseudonyms, timestamps) still supports linkage; if B1 statistically matches B4 on answerability and every RQ2 bound, CL-2 falsification fires and the receipt structure adds nothing.
mechanism_analysis: Arm B1 (registry baseline hash-only-log-digests, parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/pst/fixtures/hash_log_parity.json, exec_command registered; notes: in-project, not yet run): the RQ2 strongest competing baseline - plain hashing is the obvious argument that purpose-bound receipt structure is unnecessary. The arm must run at equal budget: if its attacker advantage with auxiliary joins statistically equals B4's while RQ1 answerability matches, the novelty contract's falsification condition fires and the claim is reported as a negative result. Implementation not yet present in evaluation/venue2027, hence UNAVAILABLE/UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN.

title: Encrypted log with role-gated decryption and deletion (blueprint arm B2; registry baseline encrypted-log-role-gated-deletion)
algorithm_class: AEAD-encrypted full audit log with per-epoch data keys, role-gated decrypt and key-deletion-based erasure
supported_guarantee: Strongest confidentiality comparator: ciphertext retains full forensic utility for authorized decryptors while denying everything to keyless readers; per-epoch data keys make key deletion a retention-decay instrument - the study-level falsification arm (CL-9).
limitations_vs_candidate: Dominant competing explanation: if B2 with a well-managed retention policy dominates B4 on RQ1 answerability and RQ2 exposure bounds simultaneously at comparable cost (RQ3), the superiority claim of ReceiptMin is rejected; key custody (declared externality X2) and per-epoch key management costs are the open question RQ3 measures.
mechanism_analysis: Arm B2 (registry baseline encrypted-log-role-gated-deletion, parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/pst/fixtures/encrypted_log_parity.json, exec_command registered; notes: in-project, not yet run): the RQ1 strongest competing baseline and the study-level falsification rule's subject - encryption plus managed retention is the established practice that could make minimized receipts pointless. The mechanism differs structurally from B4: B2 defers protection to key custody, B4 to content removal at commit time, so the frontier between them (post-decay recovery, key-loss behavior, retained bytes) is an empirical question that only a run can settle; the arm is honestly UNAVAILABLE/UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN until implemented.

title: RFC 9162-like Merkle append-only integrity with authorized material retrieval (blueprint arm B3; registry baseline ct-merkle-append-only-integrity)
venue: CLARA 2027 PST blueprint (FAITHFUL_PORT of IETF RFC 9162)
algorithm_class: Certificate Transparency v2.0-style Merkle append-only log with STHs and inclusion proofs, plus authorized material retrieval side-channel
supported_guarantee: Strongest integrity baseline: tamper-evident Merkle append-only log per RFC 9162 Sec. 2.1 (inclusion proofs Sec. 2.1.3, consistency proofs Sec. 2.1.4) with an authorized retrieval channel for material; a protocol port of the RFC's log/monitor semantics.
limitations_vs_candidate: Integrity is not confidentiality: entries are readable by design (RFC 9162 Sec. 8.1.4 flags proof-fetching as a privacy concern), no retention schedule or purpose binding exists, and the authorized-retrieval channel reintroduces exactly the exposure ReceiptMin removes - the CL-1 falsification arm.
mechanism_analysis: Arm B3 (registry baseline ct-merkle-append-only-integrity, parity fixture evaluation/venue2027/pst/fixtures/ct_merkle_parity.json, exec_command registered): a FAITHFUL_PORT of RFC 9162 log semantics - upstream revision pinned to the RFC text SHA256 a0e432ce7580c99fcc8faf0cf3f6191f9ce6b4864f949158e020d4ecb295081f (recomputed live from rfc-editor.org rfc9162.txt on 2026-11-15, matching the shared baseline registry), with certificate-transparency-go (verified live, ORIGINAL_UPSTREAM row above) as the reference implementation the port follows. Mechanistically the Merkle tree makes silent edits detectable but the leaf payload stays fully readable - the port must preserve exactly that integrity-without-confidentiality split so the CL-1 falsification test (B3 matching B4 on both axes) is run against real transparency semantics.

title: Proposed purpose-bound minimized receipt and retention map (blueprint arm B4; candidate, not a comparator)
algorithm_class: Candidate: HMAC-bound purpose/epoch commitment receipt that preserves event commitment and consent/policy-epoch proofs while dropping patient detail, plus a per-field retention map declaring scheduled decay
supported_guarantee: Claimed (not yet demonstrated): measurable reconstruction-versus-linkability frontier - commitment and epoch proofs survive retention deadlines while sensitive content decays; bounds on RQ2 attacker advantage under a compromised read-only reader with auxiliary joins; costs measured in RQ3.
limitations_vs_candidate: It is the candidate itself, not a comparator: until PST-baselines/candidate tasks land, no artifact exists and every guarantee is a prospective design commitment under the frozen novelty contract; this row exists for falsification transparency, never to assert results or to present the receipt format as an access-control mechanism.
mechanism_analysis: Candidate arm B4 recorded for falsification transparency: the mechanism (preserve commitment and consent/policy-epoch proofs while removing patient detail; retention map decays readable content per epoch) is exactly what B0-B3 must fail to deliver jointly, and the study-level falsification rule (B2 dominance) or the CL-2 condition (B1 equivalence) rejects the claim if they do not. B4 is an evaluation instrument, not a new access-control or authorization enforcement mechanism - authorization semantics remain the existing CLARA RBAC/consent systems (novelty-contract boundary X5) - and until the candidate implementation exists in evaluation/venue2027/pst/ the honest status is UNAVAILABLE_NOT_RUN.
